title: Vertebrates and Invertebrates
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Vertebrates and Invertebrates Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Animals are classified into vertebrates (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals) and invertebrates (insects, spiders, mollusks, worms and others) using their features. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 6, Quarter 2: Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Living Things): biodiversity and groups, vertebrates, invertebrates, plants and fungi, classification keys and sorting living things. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Scientists group living things by features.
key_sub: Vertebrates have a backbone; keys split groups in two at each step.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biodiversity is the variety of living things. Classification sorts them into groups by shared features.

  • Kingdoms include animals, plants and fungi (and tiny living things like bacteria).
  • Vertebrates have a backbone: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
  • Invertebrates have no backbone: insects, spiders, worms, snails.
  • A dichotomous key asks yes-or-no questions to name a living thing.
Example

A frog has moist skin and starts life as a tadpole. Which group is it in?

moist skin

water then land

Answer: amphibians

Example

Is a spider an insect?

count the legs: 8

Answer: no, it is an arachnid

Common mistakes

  • Thinking spiders are insects.
  • Thinking whales are fish (they are mammals).
  • Thinking fungi are plants.

faq.a: The variety of living things in an area, from tiny insects to large trees and animals.

faq.q: What is the difference between vertebrates and invertebrates?
faq.a: Vertebrates have a backbone. Invertebrates do not.

faq.q: How does a dichotomous key work?
faq.a: It gives two choices at each step. You choose the one that fits until you reach the name.

items.q: Which group does a harvestman belong to?
items.e: Harvestmen have 8 legs: arachnids.

items.q: Which feature do all insects share?
c: six legs and three body parts
items.e: Spiders have eight legs, so they are not insects.

items.q: Which group does an owl belong to?
items.e: An owl is a bird.

items.q: Which group of living things does the bacteria that cause food poisoning belong to?
items.e: Bacteria are living things too small to be seen without a microscope.

items.q: An animal has moist skin and its young live in water and breathe with gills. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of amphibians.

items.q: An animal has eight legs and two body parts. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of arachnids.

items.q: Which group does a salamander belong to?
items.e: A salamander is an amphibian.

items.q: Which group of living things does a moss belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which group does a grasshopper belong to?
items.e: A grasshopper is an insect.

items.q: Which group does a snail belong to?
items.e: A snail is a mollusc.

items.q: A dichotomous key gives two choices at each step. What do you do?
c: pick the choice that matches the living thing and follow it
items.e: Each step splits the group in two.

items.q: Which group does a scorpion belong to?
items.e: A scorpion is an arachnid.

items.q: Which kingdom makes its own food using sunlight?
items.e: Plants are producers.

items.q: An animal has a soft body and often a shell. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of molluscs.

items.q: Mushrooms do not make their own food and grow from spores. Which kingdom are they in?
items.e: Fungi absorb food from what they grow on.

items.q: Which group does an eel belong to?
items.e: Eels have gills and fins: fish.

items.q: An animal has a soft body and moves on a muscular foot. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of molluscs.

items.q: An animal has a hard outer skeleton, two pairs of antennae and lots of legs. Which group does it belong to?
items.e: This is a key characteristic of crustaceans.

items.q: Which group of living things does a frog belong to?
items.e: Animals feed on other living things and most can move from place to place.

items.q: Which group of living things does a money plant belong to?
items.e: Plants are green and make their own food.

items.q: Which of these animals is a mollusc?
items.e: A squid has a soft body: a mollusc.

items.q: Is a goldfish a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A goldfish is a fish.

items.q: What is biodiversity?
c: the variety of living things in an area
the number of rocks in an area
items.e: More kinds of living things means more biodiversity.

items.q: Is a lizard a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A lizard is a reptile.

items.q: Which group are spiders in?
items.e: Spiders have two body parts and eight legs.

items.q: Is a tortoise a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A tortoise is a reptile.

items.q: Is a newt a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A newt is an amphibian.

items.q: Is a beetle a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A beetle is an insect.

items.q: Is a whale a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. Whales breathe air with lungs and feed their young on milk, so they are mammals.

items.q: Which group of mammals does the sugar glider belong to?
items.e: A marsupial is a mammal whose young grow in a pouch.

items.q: Which of these animals is a mammal?
items.e: Whales breathe air with lungs and feed their young on milk, so they are mammals.

items.q: Which animal is an invertebrate?
items.e: Invertebrates have no backbone.

items.q: Which of these animals is a mammal?
items.e: A rabbit is a mammal.

items.q: Which of these animals is an insect?
items.e: A grasshopper is an insect.

items.q: Is a mussel a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
items.e: Vertebrates have a backbone; invertebrates do not. A mussel is a mollusc.

items.q: Which of these animals is an insect?
items.e: A bee is an insect.

items.q: Which tree is a conifer?
items.e: Conifers have cones and needles.

items.q: Which of these animals is a mammal?
items.e: A mole is a mammal.

items.q: A spring peeper lives in water as a tadpole and on land as an adult. Which group is it in?
items.e: Amphibians change from water to land.

items.q: Why do scientists classify living things?
c: to group them by shared features so they are easier to study
items.e: Classification shows how living things are related.

items.q: Is a horse chestnut tree a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A horse chestnut tree makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: Is a narra tree a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A narra tree makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: Is a liverwort a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A liverwort does not make flowers. It reproduces with spores.

items.q: Is a holly a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A holly makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: An animal has feathers. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has feathers belongs to the birds.

items.q: How many legs does a crab have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: Is a fir tree a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A fir tree does not make flowers. It reproduces with seeds in cones.

items.q: How many legs does a snail have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: Is a grass a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A grass makes flowers and seeds (grass and wheat have small green flowers).

items.q: Which group of animals does a beetle belong to?
items.e: A beetle has three body parts and six legs, so it belongs to the insects.

items.q: Which group of animals does a cockroach belong to?
items.e: A cockroach has three body parts and six legs, so it belongs to the insects.

items.q: Which group of animals does a bat belong to?
items.e: A bat flies but has fur and feeds its young with milk, so it is a mammal, not a bird.

items.q: Is a rose a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A rose makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: An animal has three body parts and six legs. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that has three body parts and six legs belongs to the insects.

items.q: An animal lays eggs with hard shells. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that lays eggs with hard shells belongs to the birds.

items.q: Which group of animals does a tortoise belong to?
items.e: A tortoise has dry, scaly skin, so it belongs to the reptiles.

items.q: Is a sunflower a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A sunflower makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: How many legs does a beetle have?
items.e: Counting legs is a quick way to group minibeasts: insects 6, spiders 8.

items.q: An animal feeds its young with milk. Which group does it most likely belong to?
items.e: An animal that feeds its young with milk belongs to the mammals.

items.q: Is a bluebell a flowering or a non-flowering plant?
items.e: A bluebell makes flowers and seeds.

items.q: Why do scientists use characteristics rather than habitat to classify animals?
c: Animals in the same habitat can be very different, such as a shark and a whale.
items.e: Shared features show relationships.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: shark, clownfish, catfish, dugong?
items.e: The others are fish. A dugong belongs to the mammals.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: catfish, parrot, hornbill, sparrow?
items.e: The others are birds. A catfish belongs to the fish.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong with the others: cod, goldfish, harvestman, salmon?
items.e: The other three are fish; a harvestman is one of the arachnids.

items.q: Two animals reach the same end of a key. What does this show?
c: The key needs another question to separate them.
items.e: Improve the key.

items.q: Why might two scientists classify the same plant differently at first?
c: They might choose different characteristics to group by.
items.e: Classification is based on chosen features.

items.q: Which animal does NOT belong to the same group as the others: bat, cow, goat, frog?
items.e: The others are mammals. A frog belongs to the amphibians.
